diagram_math_checks.objects: Five modes for the same real random-variable sequence X_n and target X on one probability space; 1 <= p < q <= infinity. Nodes are predicates, arrows are logical implications, not morphisms.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Local definitions def-convergence-in-lp-for-random-variables, def-convergence-in-probability, def-almost-sure-convergence-of-random-variables, and def-convergence-in-distribution-for-real-random-variables were read. Since p<q<=infinity, p is finite, matching the local Lp-to-probability theorem.

thm-lq-convergence-implies-lp-convergence-on-a-probability-space Statement and steps 1.1-2.1 give norm_p(X_n-X) <= norm_q(X_n-X) on a probability space, including q=infinity. Source line 25 supplies the same direction.
thm-lp-convergence-implies-convergence-in-probability steps 1.1-2.1 use P(|X_n-X|>epsilon) <= epsilon^(-p) E|X_n-X|^p. This matches the finite p forced by the diagram hypothesis.

thm-almost-sure-convergence-implies-convergence-in-probability steps 1.1-2.1 apply dominated convergence to threshold indicators bounded by one. This is the separate vertical incoming branch in original source line 26.
thm-convergence-in-probability-implies-convergence-in-distribution steps 1.1-2.1 squeeze CDF values at continuity points using the vanishing fixed-threshold error probability.

diagram_math_checks.relation: in distribution --dashed--> in probability, only for an almost surely constant limit
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original line 26 states this exception. thm-convergence-in-distribution-to-a-constant-is-convergence-in-probability Statement and steps 1.1-2.1 show that CDF convergence at c-epsilon and c+epsilon bounds the error probability by a sum tending to zero; replacing X by its almost surely equal constant leaves both law and error probabilities unchanged. The label and introductory prose explicitly restrict this reverse arrow.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Counterexample correspondence and absence of extra reversals
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original lines 28-37 are unchanged. For finite p<q, the q-spike has p-moment (n+1)^(p/q-1) tending to zero and q-moment one; the p-spike has p-moment one while its shrinking support gives almost-sure/probability convergence. For the symmetric-law example |(-X)-X|=2 almost surely. For independent indicators the probabilities tend to zero but their divergent sum gives infinitely many ones almost surely. The typewriter separately excludes Lp -> almost surely, and the unit-expectation spikes are expressly separate from the arrows. No negative arrow or general reverse implication is drawn.

diagram_math_checks.proof_independence: The diagram only restates existing implications; all original content is retained exactly and the final prose states that the diagram does not replace proofs.
